newsitem.title: USA: Riady family planned to buy big Calif. bank - Times.
newsitem.headline: Riady family planned to buy big Calif. bank - Times.

text.p: Indonesia's Riady family had plans to buy a multi-billion dollar bank in California before they became involved in investigations into foreign donations to the Democratic Party, the New York Times reported on Thursday.

The newspaper, which cited the family's business associates in Hong Kong, said the Riadys backed away from the plan out of concern that their links to China and regulatory problems at other U.S. banks they owned would make the purchase part of a probe into alleged Asian influence-peddling in Washington.
The Riady family, which has close ties to President Bill Clinton, has been associated with an inquiry into questionable campaign-finance contributions.
According to the Riadys' business associates in Hong Kong, the family planned to buy a new bank in California where James Riady already owned a small Los Angeles bank, the paper said.
They intended to invest hundreds of million of dollars in the bank, the paper said. The Times, which said no formal offer was ever made, did not name a specific bank.
White House special counsel Lanny Davis was quoted in the report as saying "we did not have the ability today" to say if the Clintons knew of the Riadys' attempts to buy a bank.
John Muncy, the executive vice president of the Hong Kong Chinese Bank, was the architect of the acquisition, the newspaper said.
Hong Kong Chinese Bank is jointly owned by the Riadys and China Resources, one of China's largest state-owned trading companies.
Muncy was quoted as saying the Chinese government would not have been an initial investor in the bank and the Riadys' Chinese partners would not have had a part in managing it.
But the family never made an official offer to a particular bank, the Times said.

"They have been looking for some time to expand their California operation, to strengthen their position in the Pacific Rim, which is the key channel of trade for overseas Chinese family," one associate in Asia was quoted as saying.
Those mentioned at the Hong Kong Chinese Bank and in Indonesia could not be reached for comment on the report.
